title: LP7-257: full leaf tables and seven-input windows, Q = O(2^((7/10) sqrt n)), S_C = O(2^((9/10) sqrt n)), T = O(2^((257/100) sqrt n)), O(n) qubits

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single LP7-257 algorithm and configuration of proof.md (finite exhaustive branch for n < 2^28; otherwise r0 = ceil(sqrt n), w = floor(1799 r0/2000), y7 = ceil(2491 r0/10000), Hb = ceil(1869 r0/1000), a collimation tree of eight binary levels and then y7 seven-input levels with measured windows, listed by a guess-and-chunk dissection, with leaf and merge tables of about 2^w entries, the free-frequency odd-part decoder and the controlled-shift 2-adic part) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, discards and aborts, its total charged sequential work is T(N,s) = O(2^((257/100) sqrt n)), with an absolute constant. The stronger main-branch bound is T = O(n^7 2^(2.5684 sqrt n)). The uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = 2^((257/100) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the classical-memory, quantum-memory and sample bounds of the other claims.

For the same LP7-257 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), peak classical memory on every execution branch is S_C(N,s) = O(2^((9/10) sqrt n)) bits, with an absolute constant, including depth-first merge tables, enumeration chunks and decoder records. The stronger main-branch bound is S_C = O(n^2 2^(0.8995 sqrt n)). The envelope B_C(n) = 2^((9/10) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work, quantum-memory and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LP7-257 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), peak quantum memory on every execution branch is S_Q(N,s) = O(n) qubits, with an absolute constant, including the depth-first index registers and all ancillas. The envelope B_Q(n) = n has growth index exactly 0. This holds jointly with the stated work, classical-memory and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LP7-257 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch, including every discarded copy and every failed or aborted attempt, is O(2^((7/10) sqrt n)), with an absolute constant. The stronger main-branch bound is Q <= n Ccap + K = O(n^3 2^(0.6994 sqrt n)), with Ccap and K defined in proof.md. The uniform bit-length envelope B_samples(n) = 2^((7/10) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work, classical-memory and quantum-memory bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LP7-257 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
